page: Amazon Web Services r6a.large is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of memory per physical core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25%, reflecting the physical single-core limitation. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor results, with read-only small block cached bandwidth in the bottom 10% and large block write bandwidth in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while database operations and Redis SET operations score in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r6a.large provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on dedicated AMD hardware, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel compute scaling. Given the poor multi-core scaling and low database operation benchmarks, this instance is best suited for lightweight caching layers, basic text processing, single-threaded applications, and memory-intensive development environments rather than heavy database workloads or parallelized compilation tasks.
